taxonomic_note: Accepted by current treatments. Modern Croton section Heptallon work recognizes infraspecific structure; this learner remains at species rank unless local material is confidently assigned below species.
look_here_first: Start with the low branching habit and the pistillate flower. This is a small annual often branching from the base; the lower leaf surface lacks the brown-dot effect of Croton monanthogynus, and three bifid styles give six terminal segments.

project_inclusion.range_basis: A modern revision of Croton section Heptallon documents representative C. lindheimerianus var. lindheimerianus material from Llano (Enchanted Rock), Medina (near Devine), and Travis (Austin/Colorado River), all inside the project target zone.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Do not reuse the previously considered Williamson evidence for the project threshold; the locked three-county set is Llano, Medina, and Travis.

best_field_traits: lower leaf surface lacks the dark brown-dot effect of C. monanthogynus
pistillate sepals usually 5–6 and broadest toward their tips
three bifid styles yielding six terminal segments
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Croton monanthogynus has dark-centered stellate hairs that create a brown-dotted lower leaf surface, two styles/four terminal branches, and an effectively one-seeded fruit. Croton lindheimeri is generally more robust with much larger yellowish-woolly pistillate sepals.

comparisons.key_distinctions: No brown-dot effect beneath the leaves plus three bifid styles/six terminal branches separate C. lindheimerianus from C. monanthogynus; its smaller pistillate sepals help separate it from C. lindheimeri.
